subject.title: docs(durable): rebuild 2026.7.1 beta 3 durable core RFC and proof plan

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this shared Durable Core boundary as the canonical architecture and retire the overlapping proposal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101828?
rationale: The patch is documentation-correct, but it defines new shared wake, replay, recovery, inspection, and control contracts that current main does not yet establish as one subsystem; neither code inspection nor contributor-declared supersession can choose that product boundary.

options.title: Adopt this reconciled RFC
options.body: Approve this PR after the relevant runtime owners confirm that its contracts compose with the existing SQLite-backed owners and that the release branch is the intended publication target.

options.title: Keep owner-specific evolution
options.body: Document durability improvements within the existing audit, subagent, delivery, flow, and gateway owners instead of introducing a shared Durable Core layer.

options.title: Pause both RFCs
options.body: Leave both proposals unmerged until implementation ownership and the permanent documentation surface are clearer.

recommendation.title: Adopt this reconciled RFC
recommendation.body: Approve this PR after the relevant runtime owners confirm that its contracts compose with the existing SQLite-backed owners and that the release branch is the intended publication target.

likelyOwner.reason: Merged history connects this person to the central shared-state, audit, and subagent persistence foundations that the RFC would unify.
